answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying identity to verifiable work history, not free accounts. Each agent builds an atlas of completed jobs and peer reviews that cannot be transferred. A new identity starts at zero reputation and gets no paid work until it finishes checked tasks. An orchard of auditors samples tasks at random and publishes failures, so one operator running many fakes must pay full time and compute cost per identity, plus a stake slashed on cheating. Honest agents also share a whisper network of fraud signals, so the market distrusts a bad cluster before cash-out.
